items.question_text: You are planning to migrate your containerized workloads to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). You need to determine which GKE option to use. Your solution must have high availability, minimal downtime, and the ability to promptly apply security updates to your nodes. You also want to pay only for the compute resources that your workloads use without managing nodes. You want to follow Google-recommended practices and minimize operational costs. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Autopilot is the Google-recommended solution for workloads where you do not want to manage node infrastructure or capacity.
It automatically handles node provisioning, scaling, and patching, ensuring high availability and prompt security updates without manual intervention.
You only pay for the actual resources consumed by your pods, satisfying the requirement to avoid paying for idle node compute.

choices.text: Configure a Standard regional GKE duster.
Configure a Standard zonal GKE duster.
Configure a Standard multi-zonal GKE cluster.
Configure an Autopilot GKE cluster.

items.question_text:
Your company stores data from multiple sources that have different data storage requirements. These data include:
1. Customer data that is structured and read with complex queries
2. Historical log data that is large in volume and accessed infrequently
3. Real-time sensor data with high-velocity writes, which needs to be available for analysis but can tolerate some data loss

You need to design the most cost-effective storage solution that fulfills all data storage requirements. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Cloud SQL is the correct choice for structured customer data requiring complex queries, as Firestore is a NoSQL document database not optimized for relational joins. Cloud Storage (Archive) provides the most cost-effective solution for large volumes of infrequently accessed historical log data compared to Nearline or Coldline tiers.
Bigtable is designed for high-velocity write workloads and real-time sensor data, whereas BigQuery is an analytics warehouse not suited for sustained ultra-high ingestion rates.

choices.text: Use Firestore for customer data, Cloud Storage (Nearline) for historical logs, and Bigtable for sensor data.
Use Cloud SQL for customer data. Cloud Storage (Coldline) for historical logs, and BigQuery for sensor data.
Use Cloud SQL for customer data. Cloud Storage (Archive) for historical logs, and Bigtable for sensor data.
Use Spanner for all data.

items.question_text:
You work for a financial services company that operates as a stock market broker. Your company is planning to migrate to Google Cloud. You need to plan the network design in Google Cloud. Your design must:
• Minimize the latency between all production systems.
• Minimize costs related to your development environment.

What should you do?
items.solution_text:
To minimize latency for production systems, you should deploy them in the Premium Tier, which leverages Google's global, high-performance backbone network.

To minimize costs for the development environment, you should use the Standard Tier, as it has lower egress pricing and is suitable for non-latency-critical workloads.

choices.text: Create a VPC in the Standard Tier and one in the Premium Tier. Deploy production workloads in the Standard Tier and development workloads in the Premium Tier.
Create a VPC in the Standard Tier and one in the Premium Tier. Deploy development workloads in the Standard Tier and production workloads in the Premium Tier.
Create a VPC in the Premium Tier, and deploy both production and development workloads on this VPC.
Create a VPC in the Standard Tier, and deploy both production and development workloads on this VPC.

items.question_text: You are managing a fleet of Compute Engine Linux instances in a Google Cloud project. Your company's engineering team requires SSH access to all instances to perform routine maintenance tasks. You need to manage the SSH access for the engineering team, and you want to minimize operational overhead when engineers join or leave the team. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Option D is correct because OS Login maps IAM permissions to SSH access, eliminating the need for manual key management.
By using a Google Group and managing membership within it, administrative overhead is minimized when engineers join or leave the team.
Options A and B require manual maintenance of SSH keys, while Option C only grants viewing rights without enabling actual SSH connectivity.

choices.text: Create a single SSH key pair to be shared by all engineering team members. Add the public SSH key to project metadata.
Create an SSH key pair for each engineer on the team, and add the public SSH key to the metadata of the relevant instances.
Create a Google Group for all engineering team members, and grant them the Compute Viewer IAM role. Manage group membership when engineers join or leave the team.
Create a Google Group for all engineering team members, and set up OS Login for this group on the project. Manage group membership when engineers join or leave the team.

items.question_text: Your company was recently impacted by a service disruption that caused multiple Dataflow jobs to get stuck, resulting in significant downtime in downstream applications and revenue loss. You were able to resolve the issue by identifying and fixing an error you found in the code. You need to design a solution with minimal management effort to identify when jobs are stuck in the future to ensure that this issue does not occur again. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Option B is the correct choice because it utilizes native Cloud Monitoring alerts on the built-in 'data freshness' metric, which directly detects when Dataflow jobs fall behind or get stuck.

This approach requires minimal management effort as it leverages automatic metric collection without custom code or complex infrastructure like Pub/Sub topics and Cloud Tasks (Option A).

Error Reporting (Option C) only captures stack traces from crashes, not logical stalls, while the Service Health dashboard (Option D) reflects Google's service uptime rather than specific job performance issues.

choices.text: Update the Dataflow job configurations to send messages to a Pub/Sub topic when there are delays. Configure a backup Dataflow job to process jobs that are delayed. Use Cloud Tasks to trigger an alert when messages are pushed to the Pub/Sub topic.
Set up Cloud Monitoring alerts on the data freshness metric for the Dataflow jobs to receive a notification when a certain threshold is reached.
Set up Error Reporting to identify stack traces that indicate slowdowns in Dataflow jobs. Set up alerts based on these log entries.
Use the Personalized Service Health dashboard to identify issues with Dataflow jobs across regions.
